title: Problem 1.1
statement_text: Given a fixed $k$-uniform hypergraph $G$, determine the integer $h$ (if it exists) such that $r(G;q)$ grows as a tower of height $h$ as $q$ tends to infinity.
context_text: For a $k$-uniform hypergraph ($k$-graph) $G$, the $q$-color Ramsey number $r(G;q)$ is the minimum $N$ such that every coloring of the edges of the complete $k$-graph $K_N^{(k)}$ with $q$ colors contains a monochromatic copy of $G$. The tower function is $\mathrm{tw}_1(x)=x$ and $\mathrm{tw}_h(x)=2^{\mathrm{tw}_{h-1}(x)}$, and a function $f(q)$ grows as a tower of height $h$ if $\mathrm{tw}_h(\Omega(q^c))\le f(q)\le\mathrm{tw}_h(O(q^C))$ for some constants $c,C>0$. Not every function grows as a tower of some height, but it may be natural to guess that $r(G;q)$ always does. For graphs, $r(G;q)$ grows as a tower of height $1$ if $G$ is bipartite with at least two edges and as a tower of height $2$ otherwise. For $3$-graphs, Abbott and Williams showed that $r(K_4^{(3)};q)$ grows as a tower of height $3$, and Axenovich, Gyárfás, Liu and Mubayi showed that $r(G;q)$ is polynomial if and only if $G$ is tripartite and asked which $3$-graphs have double-exponential $r(G;q)$. The authors resolve the problem for $k=3$: they define an explicit nested family of classes $\mathcal{U}$ of $3$-graphs (via collapsing vertex sets that no edge meets in exactly two vertices) and show that for every $3$-graph $G$ with at least two edges, $r(G;q)$ grows as a tower of height $1$ if $G$ is tripartite, of height $2$ if $G\in\mathcal{U}$ is not tripartite, and of height $3$ otherwise. For higher uniformities the problem is open; the authors tentatively conjecture that $r(G;q)$ grows as a tower of some height for every fixed uniform hypergraph $G$, and do not know the answer even for the $4$-graph on $A\cup B$ ($|A|=|B|=t\ge3$) whose edges are the $4$-sets meeting $A$ and $B$ in two vertices each (it is between exponential and double exponential).
paper_title: The growth rate of multicolor Ramsey numbers of $3$-graphs

title: Problem 1.2 (Axenovich, Gyárfás, Hong and Mubayi)
statement_text: For which $3$-uniform hypergraphs $G$, is $r(G;q)$ double exponential? Are there other jumps that the Ramsey function exhibits?
context_text: This question was posed by Axenovich, Gyárfás, Hong and Mubayi in their 2014 study of multicolor Ramsey numbers for triple systems. The present paper identifies it as the central open problem motivating the work and resolves it completely for 3-uniform hypergraphs.
paper_contribution: Fully resolves the problem by proving that for every non-tripartite 3-uniform hypergraph $G$, either $2^{\Omega(q)} < r(G;q) < 2^{q^C}$ for some $C=C(G)$, or $2^{2^{q/2}} < r(G;q)$, and characterizes exactly which 3-graphs fall into each class.
notes: The abstract refers to the fourth author as 'Liu' while the bibliography [4] lists 'L. Hong'; these likely refer to the same person (Liu Hong).
paper_title: The growth rate of multicolor Ramsey numbers of $3$-graphs

title: Problem 4.1
statement_text: Does there exist, for every $\ell\geq 1,$ a $3$-uniform hypergraph $G_{\ell}$ with $r(G_{\ell};q)=2^{q^{\ell+o(1)}}$?
context_text: For a $k$-uniform hypergraph ($k$-graph) $G$, the $q$-color Ramsey number $r(G;q)$ is the minimum $N$ such that every coloring of the edges of the complete $k$-graph $K_N^{(k)}$ with $q$ colors contains a monochromatic copy of $G$. The tower function is $\mathrm{tw}_1(x)=x$ and $\mathrm{tw}_h(x)=2^{\mathrm{tw}_{h-1}(x)}$, and a function $f(q)$ grows as a tower of height $h$ if $\mathrm{tw}_h(\Omega(q^c))\le f(q)\le\mathrm{tw}_h(O(q^C))$ for some constants $c,C>0$. In a $3$-graph $G$, a set $U\subseteq V(G)$ with $2\le|U|<|V(G)|$ is collapsible if no edge meets $U$ in exactly two vertices; collapsing $U$ gives the $3$-graph $H$ on $(V(G)\setminus U)\cup\{v^*\}$ whose edges are the edges of $G$ disjoint from $U$ and the triples $xyv^*$ such that $xyu\in E(G)$ for some $u\in U$, and $G$ is then reducible to $(H,G[U])$. $\mathcal{U}_0$ is the class of tripartite $3$-graphs, $\mathcal{U}_1$ the class of $3$-graphs having a vertex set meeting every edge in exactly one vertex, and for $i>1$, $\mathcal{U}_i$ is the largest class containing $\mathcal{U}_{i-1}$ and every $3$-graph reducible to some $(H,F)$ with $H\in\mathcal{U}_{i-1}$ and $F\in\mathcal{U}_i$; $\mathcal{U}=\bigcup_i\mathcal{U}_i$. The authors prove that for a $3$-graph $G$ with at least two edges, $r(G;q)=q^{\Theta(1)}$ if $G\in\mathcal{U}_0$; $2^{\Omega(q)}\le r(G;q)\le2^{O(q^\ell\log q)}$ if $G\in\mathcal{U}_\ell\setminus\mathcal{U}_0$; and $2^{2^{q/2}}\le r(G;q)\le2^{2^{O(q\log q)}}$ if $G\notin\mathcal{U}$. So for non-tripartite $G\in\mathcal{U}$ the lower and upper bounds often have different powers of $q$ in the exponent. Writing $\mathrm{Star}^{(3)}(h)$ for the $3$-graph on $h$ vertices whose edges are all triples containing a fixed vertex, it is easy to see that $r(\mathrm{Star}^{(3)}(4);q)=2^{q^{1+o(1)}}$, and the authors construct a $3$-graph $G$ with $r(G;q)=2^{q^{2+o(1)}}$ (blow up a non-central vertex of $\mathrm{Star}^{(3)}(4)$ into a set of $4$ vertices spanning a copy of $\mathrm{Star}^{(3)}(4)$). For each $\ell\ge3$ there are $3$-graphs $G_\ell$ for which their best upper bound is of the form $2^{q^{\ell+o(1)}}$, and they ask whether this can be tight. Even for the Fano plane only $2^{\Omega(q)}\le r(\mathrm{Fano};q)\le2^{O(q^2\log q)}$ is known.
paper_title: The growth rate of multicolor Ramsey numbers of $3$-graphs
